headline: Spain Creates 23 New Marine Protected Areas Spanning 22,405 km²
meta_description: Spain proposes 23 new marine protected areas around the Canary Islands and Mediterranean coasts to safeguard seagrass meadows, reefs, and submarine canyons.
summary_short: Spain is establishing 23 new marine protected areas covering over 22,000 km² across the Canary Islands and Mediterranean, targeting vulnerable ocean ecosystems.
body:
Spain has proposed 23 new marine protected areas spanning 22,405 km² around the Canary Islands and Mediterranean coasts—a significant expansion of ocean conservation across two of Europe's most biodiverse marine regions.

The protected zones focus on three critical ecosystems: seagrass meadows, reefs, and submarine canyons. These underwater landscapes harbor extraordinary biodiversity and play essential roles in carbon storage and fish breeding. By safeguarding them from overfishing and industrial activity, Spain aims to restore balance to waters that have faced decades of pressure.

The proposal reflects growing recognition that protecting marine life requires thinking beyond land. Submarine canyons—deep underwater valleys carved into the continental shelf—support unique species found nowhere else on Earth. Similarly, seagrass meadows and reef systems anchor entire food webs that sustain both wild populations and human fishing communities. Spain's comprehensive approach to protecting these three habitat types suggests a thoughtful strategy rooted in ecological science rather than piecemeal conservation.
quick_facts: Spain proposes 23 new marine protected areas
Total coverage: 22,405 km² across two regions
Located around Canary Islands and Mediterranean coasts
Protects seagrass meadows, reefs, submarine canyons
